subject: aspirin
correct: Aspirin 75–150 mg daily from 12 weeks until birth if ONE high-risk factor or MORE THAN ONE moderate-risk factor (NICE NG133 1.1.2–1.1.3)

fixes.old: Offer low-dose aspirin from 12 weeks until birth to women at high or moderate risk (preventive role)
fixes.new: Offer aspirin 75–150 mg daily from 12 weeks until birth to women with one high-risk factor or more than one moderate-risk factor for pre-eclampsia (NICE NG133)

note: Article implies a single moderate risk factor qualifies; NG133 requires two or more moderate factors (or any one high-risk factor).

subject: ibuprofen
correct: Ibuprofen 400 mg (adult) — 500–1000 mg is the paracetamol dose; zoledronate SPC: acute-phase symptoms reduced by paracetamol or ibuprofen shortly after the infusion

fixes.old: Prophylactic paracetamol or ibuprofen 500–1000 mg 6-hourly for 24–48 hours significantly reduces this reaction.
fixes.new: Prophylactic paracetamol (1 g 6-hourly) or ibuprofen (400 mg 8-hourly, if no contraindication) for 24–48 hours reduces this reaction.

note: Ibuprofen 500–1000 mg 6-hourly would be up to 4 g/day — far above the 2.4 g/day maximum. Only file with this sentence.

subject: amlodipine
correct: No atorvastatin 50 mg strength exists and the SPC/BNF set no atorvastatin dose cap with amlodipine; the MHRA (2012) 20 mg cap applies to simvastatin only

fixes.old: (50mg atorvastatin with amlodipine: acceptable; 80mg: caution but generally used)
fixes.new: (no atorvastatin dose restriction with amlodipine in the SPC; the MHRA 20 mg cap applies to simvastatin)

note: Invented dose (atorvastatin comes as 10/20/30/40/60/80 mg) and an invented 80 mg caution.

subject: LDL/non-HDL
correct: NICE NG238 1.7.1: LDL ≤2.0 mmol/L or non-HDL ≤2.6 mmol/L (no '≥50% reduction' criterion); the National Clinical Guideline for Stroke (<1.8 / <2.5) is quoted separately on tools/management/tia-stroke.html

fixes.old: Target LDL <2.0 mmol/L (or ≥50% reduction from baseline)
fixes.new: Target LDL ≤2.0 mmol/L or non-HDL ≤2.6 mmol/L (NICE NG238)

fixes.old: A post-treatment LDL >2.0 mmol/L (or <50% reduction) indicates
fixes.new: A post-treatment LDL >2.0 mmol/L (or non-HDL >2.6 mmol/L) indicates

note: Every other page uses ≤2.0/≤2.6 (NG238). The TIA case uses <2.0 and adds a ≥50% criterion; the PAD case adds '<50% reduction'. Neither is in NG238.

subject: LDL/non-HDL
correct: FH (NICE CG71): aim for at least a 50% LDL-C reduction from the untreated baseline; there is no NICE absolute LDL target of <2.5 mmol/L

fixes.old: Target: ≥50% reduction in LDL-C from untreated baseline (or LDL-C <2.5 mmol/L in adults)
fixes.new: Target: ≥50% reduction in LDL-C from untreated baseline (NICE CG71)

note: The '<2.5 mmol/L' is not NICE and appears nowhere else on the site (the FH protocol uses ≥50% only).
